MEMORANDUM ON THE CASE OF
BOEN DJIE-PO AND TJONG KHIE-TJHONG.
SECRET - NOT FOR PUBLICATION.

In 1911 an arrangement was arrived at between the Netherlands
and the Chinese Governments to the effect that persons born in the
Netherlands Colonies from parents established there, will if they
travel to China, be considered Netherlands subjects provided they
register themselves as such with a Netherlands Consulate within
three months upon their arrival in China. The Consular officer con-
cerned gives notice of this registration to the local authorities,
at Shanghai to those of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai and of
the International Settlement and the French Concession, whilst the
Netherlands Legation sends the names of the persons so registered
to the Chinese Central Government.

These registrations are effected only after complete documen-
tary evidence has been produced by the applicants in support of
their statements.

Some time ago two students (A) Boen Djie-Po alias Wen Yu-eno
(温玉奴) born at Djakarta, Java, 18 years of age and (B) Tjong
Khie-tjhong alias Chang Chi-tsai (张奇才) born at Blitar, Java,
16 years of age, arrived in Shanghai and duly presented themselves
for registration at the Netherlands Consulate General at Shanghai.
They presented "Verklaringen van Inlandscherschap" (Declarations of
Nationality) issued (a) by the head of the local government of
Madiun-Kediri on 20 May 1932, No. 2042, and (b) the same authority
at Blitar on 5 June 1932, No. 214, whereas (A) had a passport No. 38
issued by the Resident of Kediri on 5 June 1932, stating both in
the declaration and in the passport documents that he was a Nether-
lands subject.

Upon receipt of application for their registration at the Consu-
late the Netherlands Consulate General at Shanghai notified the
same to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, to the Council of the

关于 BOEN DJIE-PO 和 TJONG KHIE-TJHONG 案件的备忘录。
机密 - 不得发表。

1911年，荷兰政府与中国政府达成一项安排，规定在荷兰殖民地出生、其父母定居于该地的人，若前往中国，只要在抵达中国后三个月内向荷兰领事馆注册为荷兰臣民，即被视为荷兰臣民。有关领事官员会将此注册事项通知地方当局，在上海则通知大上海市政府、公共租界及法租界的当局，同时荷兰公使馆会将此类注册人员的名单报送中国政府。

只有在申请人提供完整的书面证据以支持其陈述后，才会办理这些注册手续。

不久前，两名学生（A）Boen Djie-Po，又名 Wen Yu-eno（温玉奴），生于爪哇雅加达，18岁；（B）Tjong Khie-tjhong，又名 Chang Chi-tsai（张奇才），生于爪哇Blitar，16岁，抵达上海，并按规定前往荷兰驻上海总领事馆进行注册。他们出示了由以下机构签发的“土著国籍声明书”（Verklaringen van Inlandscherschap）：(a) Madiun-Kediri 地方政府首脑于1932年5月20日签发，编号2042；(b) Blitar 同一当局于1932年6月5日签发，编号214。此外，(A) 持有 Kediri 驻地官于1932年6月5日签发的第38号护照，声明书和护照文件均声明其为荷兰臣民。

荷兰驻上海总领事馆收到他们的注册申请后，随即通知大上海市政府及工部局董事会，

letters of 18 April 1932 and 12 November 1932, No's 1184 and 3152.

On the 30th of November a certain Boeng San-fong (黄生芳)
also a Netherlandic' subject, and a student at the Chinan school,
arrived at the above Consulate General with a letter from the two
boys, written in pencil on Chinese toilet paper, stating that they
had been arrested by the Bureau of Public Safety at the request
of the school authorities and that they were detained there for
about one month. They asked Boeng to notify the Netherlands Con-
sulate, and to borrow some money wherewith to buy food for them.

On the first of December Mr. van den Berg called on Mr. Yui
Hung-chun, the secretary of the Mayor, asking him to take immediate-
ly the necessary steps to have the boys brought to the Nether-
lands' Consulate General for hearing and to send at the same time
such evidence as could be produced to substantiate the crime for
which they had been detained.

Mr. Yui contended that according to the Chinese Nationality
Law the boys were Chinese citizens as they could not produce evi-
dence that they had obtained permission to renounce their Chinese
nationality.

It was pointed out to him that according to the arrangement
made between the former Pai Fu Pa and the Netherlands Minister
at Peking in 1921 the Chinese Government had given its formal appro-
val to the procedure whereby regularly lists were to be supplied
to the Chinese authorities of those persons who had registered
themselves with the Netherlands Consular authorities in China;
the said Pai Fu Pa's note stating : " I assume that the names of all
"persons who are Dutch subjects will be furnished to the Chinese
"authorities for information and for official notification, with
"which no objection will be raised."

Mr. Yui was told, that in order to escape nationality
law, that that law could not override an international agreement.

分别通过1932年4月18日和1932年11月12日的信函，编号1184和3152。

11月30日，另一位荷兰臣民、暨南学校的学生 Boeng San-fong（黄生芳）来到上述总领事馆，带来那两个男孩用铅笔写在中国草纸上的信，信中称他们应校方要求被公安局逮捕，并已被拘留约一个月。他们请 Boeng 通知荷兰领事馆，并借些钱为他们购买食物。

12月1日，van den Berg 先生拜访了市长秘书俞鸿钧先生，请他立即采取必要措施，将这两个男孩带到荷兰总领事馆接受讯问，并同时送交任何可提供的证据，以证实他们被拘留的罪名。

俞先生辩称，根据中国国籍法，这两个男孩是中国公民，因为他们无法提供已获得放弃中国国籍许可的证据。

有人向他指出，根据1921年前外交总长颜惠庆与荷兰驻北京公使达成的安排，中国政府已正式批准这一程序，即定期向中方当局提供在荷兰驻华领事机构注册的人员名单；颜惠庆的照会中称：“我假定所有荷兰臣民的名单都将提供给中国当局知悉并进行正式通知，对此不会提出异议。”

有人告诉俞先生，为了规避国籍法，该法律不能凌驾于国际协定之上。

He nevertheless refused to hand over the boys in question,
but promised to ask instructions from Nanking.
Two days later, 3 December, Mr.Bijvank, then acting Consul-
General, called on the Mayor, who assumed the same attitude
as Mr.Yui, and also said that he had to await instructions.
When asked for what reason the boys were detained, the Mayor
stated that they were suspected of efforts to establish a
nucleus of the Communist Youth Organisation amongst the
students of the Chinese School.
So far however not the slightest evidence to that effect
has been produced.
The matter was duly referred to the Netherlands Minister
at Peking, who telegraphed the Chinese Government on 9
December, asking that the Shanghai Authorities be instructed
to hand over the prisoners immediately to the jurisdiction
of the Netherlands Consulate-General, and on 14 December
telegraphed again to that effect. Instructions were also
received by the Netherlands Consulate General to notify the
Mayor of the steps taken by the Netherlands Minister and
to protest against the unlawful detention of the boys. On
18 December Mr.Graumann visited the acting Mayor, Mr.Yui,
and left him an aide-memoire, by way of formal protest.
It was intimated during this visit that the Bureau of Public
Safety might release the boys on security. The next day
a note was sent to the Netherlands Consulate General, signed
by the Mayor stating e.g.:
* Considering that Sun and Tjong are young and suscep-
* tible to sedition, I decided to hand them over to their
* parents for proper education. The Bureau of Public

* under a suitable guarantee for their good behaviour
* directly to them, where they are to be handed over to
* the custody of their parents. The said Bureau has now

两天后，即12月3日，时任代理总领事 Bijvank 先生拜访了市长，市长采取了与俞先生相同的态度，也表示必须等待指示。当被问及拘留男孩的原因时，市长称他们涉嫌在暨南学校学生中建立共产主义青年团的核心组织。
然而，迄今为止，尚未提出丝毫此类证据。
此事已 duly 转呈荷兰驻北京公使，公使于12月9日电告中国政府，要求指示上海当局立即将囚犯移交给荷兰总领事馆管辖，并于12月14日再次就此发电。荷兰总领事馆也收到指示，通知市长荷兰公使所采取的步骤，并对非法拘留男孩提出抗议。12月18日，Graumann 先生拜访了代理市长俞先生，并向他递交了一份备忘录，作为正式抗议。
在此次拜访期间，有人暗示公安局可能会在提供担保的情况下释放这两个男孩。次日，市长签署了一份致荷兰总领事馆的照会，其中写道：

On 16 December the boys were released and this is the
gist of their statements made to the Netherlands Consulate
General :
• Mr. Chen Hon-nien, Dean of the Chinan School decided to
separate the Middle School from the College, and to have
the Middle School split in two branches, one at Canton
and one at Soochow, whereas free tuition granted to
students taking the Normal Course in the middle school
was to be discontinued.
Opposition to this scheme was xxx raised by the students,
who were of opinion that the accommodation at Soochow
and at Canton was insufficient and that they wished to
continue the privilege granted to normal course students.
They declared a strike and the school authorities had
to give in. Born was suspected of being one of the
ringleaders of the strike and he was therefore suspended
from attending the school for a period of one year. He
subsequently had to leave the premises of the school and
took up his abode at the house of Tjang, who was studying
at the Middle School. Tjang had a quarrel with one of
his teachers on account of the latter having opened one
of the letters he had sent out, and in which he had criti-
cised the school.
On 27 October 1921, Born, whilst he was on his way home
from a visit to the school library, was attacked by plain clothes detectives
from the Bureau of Public Safety, bundled into a motor
car, and brought to the Central Station at Peking Nan.
He was accused pro hac vice and deprivation of
civil rights was asked. All his claims to immunity

• 报告称，这两个男孩已在暨南大学的担保下获释。”
12月16日，这两个男孩获释，以下是他们向荷兰总领事馆所作陈述的要点：
• 暨南学校教务长陈洪年先生决定将中学与大学分开，并将中学分为两个分部，一个在广州，一个在苏州，同时取消给予中学师范课程学生的免费学费待遇。
学生们对该方案提出了 xxx 反对，他们认为苏州和广州的住宿条件不足，并希望继续保留给予师范课程学生的特权。他们宣布罢工，校方不得不让步。Born 被怀疑是罢工的带头人物之一，因此被勒令停学一年。他随后不得不离开校舍，寄住在就读于中学的 Tjang 家中。Tjang 因其中一位老师拆阅了他寄出的一封信件而与该老师发生争执，他在信中批评了学校。
1921年10月27日，Born 在从学校图书馆回家的路上遭到公安局便衣侦探的袭击，被强行塞进一辆汽车，带至北平中央车站。
他被临时指控，并被要求剥夺公民权利。他所有的豁免权

was during all the time of his detention from 27 October

School.
Both Been and Tjeng upon their release from detention were

臣民身份主张从一开始就被无视，在10月27日至12月16日的整个拘留期间，他仅在10月29日被带上警察法庭一次，当时他被问及何时加入共产党。当他回答对此事一无所知时，又被带回拘留室。”
“Tjeng 于10月31日在学校大门附近以同样粗暴的方式被捕，也被汽车带至中央车站。他也受到搜查，文件被没收。同样，他要求被送往荷兰总领事馆的请求也被无视。11月3日，他被带上警察法庭，被问及是否加入了共产主义青年团。他否认对该组织有任何了解，随后也被带回拘留室。”
Been 和 Tjeng 的财产也在其住所被公安局没收，但迄今为止，在他们身上或别处未发现任何可能显示他们与共产党有牵连的物品。他们的财产仅在经历重重困难并在学校提供担保后才得以发还。
Been 和 Tjeng 在获释后均被学校开除。
我们就暨南学校当局致公安局要求释放他们的信函内容如下：
“获悉贵局将审议本校前学生 Been 和 Tjeng 的释放事宜，二人目前处于被捕状态。
因此我们恳请停止起诉，并希望贵局允许尽快释放这两名男孩，

they can be sent back to their home and handed over to their
parents for admonition."

There is no doubt that discipline at the Chinan School is
entirely lacking and that the students constitute an unruly
lot. Boer and Tjeng's denial that they had no part in the
troubles that were created there is hardly acceptable, but
there is no gain-saying the fact that the way in which the
school authorities handle the machinery of the Bureau of
Public Safety is bound to create a feeling of opposition
against all authority and forces hot tempered, badly paid
students into the ranks of subversive elements.

Shanghai, 24th December 1932.

Date 19/12/32

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, December 16, 1932

Netherlands Consul General
Asks Alleged Reds’ Release

Claiming that the two students of the Chinan University, Chenju, arrested by the Bureau of Public Safety as communist suspects, are Dutch citizens, Mr. F. E. H. Groenman, local Consul-General for the Netherlands, lodged a protest with the City Government of Greater Shanghai yesterday afternoon. Their handing over to the Netherlands consular authorities is demanded.

The students, Wen Yu-ho and Chang Chi-tei, are stated to have been born in Java, Netherlands East Indies and are naturalised Dutch citizens. Mr. Groenman pointed out in his document to the City Government. Arrested several days ago on charges of being communists, they should be handed over to the Netherlands consular authorities inasmuch as they enjoy extraterritorial rights, he contended.

Mr. O. K. Yui, secretary general of the City Government of Greater Shanghai, received Mr. Groenman in the absence of Mayor Wu Te-chen, who is attending the Third Plenary Session of the Kuomintang Central Executive Committee in Nanking. Mr. Yui replied that under the Chinese naturalization law, naturalization documents are held invalid unless the subject in question has previously addressed the Ministry of Interior renouncing Chinese citizenship.

In the case of the two students Mr. Yui continued, the City Government continues to consider them as Chinese citizens until they produce papers showing that their application for renunciation of Chinese citizenship are produced. The students, meanwhile, are being detained at the Bureau headquarters, Nantao, pending the outcome of the negotiations.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1932年12月16日，星期五

荷兰总领事
要求释放涉嫌赤化分子

荷兰驻本地总领事 F. E. H. Groenman 先生昨天下午向大上海市政府提出抗议，声称暨南大学的两名学生 Chenju 被公安局以共产党嫌疑犯逮捕，他们是荷兰公民。要求将他们移交给荷兰领事当局。

据称，学生 Wen Yu-ho 和 Chang Chi-tei 出生于荷属东印度爪哇，是归化的荷兰公民。Groenman 先生在致市政府的文件中指出。他辩称，他们几天前以共产党罪名被捕，鉴于他们享有治外法权，应被移交给荷兰领事当局。

大上海市政府秘书长俞鸿钧先生在市长吴铁城缺席的情况下接待了 Groenman 先生，吴市长正在南京参加国民党中央执行委员会第三届全体会议。俞先生回答说，根据中国入籍法，除非当事人此前已向内政部申请放弃中国国籍，否则入籍文件无效。

俞先生接着说，在这两名学生的案例中，市政府继续视他们为中国公民，直到他们出示表明已申请放弃中国国籍的文件为止。与此同时，这两名学生被拘留在南市公安局总部，等待谈判结果。
